 6m ago 09.28 EST Alvaro Arbeloa: Fulham’s head coach could scarcely be more pleased and is taking the time to give each of his players in turn a big post-match hug. He has also milked the applause of Fulham’s travelling fans, who will be able to enjoy their chesseboards, hummus and carrot batons on the journey home.
 Share 8m ago 09.26 EST Manchester City 1-1 Fulham
 Premier League: The points are shared at the Etihad Stadium, where a fine equaliser from Elliot Anderson cancelled out Rodrigo Muniz’s outstanding opener. Manchester City’s fans aren’t happy with their team, who weren’t anywhere near their best this afternoon but at least managed to avoid defeat.
 Fulham were outstanding, particularly in defence and will feel they should have taken all three points. On the plus side, they have at least managed to put an end to the winning streak City have enjoyed at their expense, a run of 20 consecutive defeats dating back to 2011.
 Share 12m ago 09.22 EST 90+3 min: We’re in the final minute of added time and that winner I predicted no longer looks like coming. On cue, referee Tom Brammall blows the final whistle and the match ends in a draw.
 Share 13m ago 09.20 EST 90+2 min: Cherki advances into the Fulham box and tries to create and angle for a shot. Sander Berge and Antonee Robinson combine to put a stop to his gallop.
 Share 14m ago 09.19 EST 90+1 min: Fulham lay siege to the City box and Sander Berge pulls the ball across the face of goal from the byline. There’s nobody in a red shirt suitably placed to convert.
 Share 15m ago 09.18 EST 90 min: In a sight you don’t see too often, Jeremy Doku is penalised for a foul throw deep in Fulham territory.
 Share 16m ago 09.17 EST 89 min: Sander Berge plays a long ball towards the left side of the City penalty area, where Gonzalo Garcia wins it after Ruben Dias had misjudged its flight. City manage to clear their lines regardless.
 Share 18m ago 09.16 EST 87 min: Cherki robs the ball from Palacios and charges upfield from inside his own half before yielding possession back to Fulham . I have a feeling in my bones we might get a winner before this match ends but I couldn’t say which team will score it.
 Share 19m ago 09.14 EST 85 min: Affengruber is on hand to cut out a low Fernandez cross into the Fulham penalty areas that was heading towards Haaland at the far post. The flag goes up for an offside.
 Share 21m ago 09.13 EST 84 min: Erling Haaland raises his arms in sarcastic celebration after finally getting a free-kick for a foul on him by David Affengruber. Man City substitution: Enzo Fernandez on for Bouaddi.
 Share 22m ago 09.11 EST 82 min: Following good work from Haaland and Allan, Rayan Cherki has a low shot blocked at close range by Calvin Bassey. Fulham double substitution: Tom Cairney on for Muniz and Cesar Palacios on for Sessegnon.
 Share 24m ago 09.09 EST 80 min: Manchester City substitution from three minutes ago: Allan Elias is on for Iliman Ndiaye.
 Share 26m ago 09.08 EST 79 min: Kenny Tete runs into Gvardiol as he tries to advance down the right wing and the ball goes out for a Fulham throw-in.
 Share 27m ago 09.06 EST 77 min: Both sides feel they can win this game and Fulham show their intent by bringing the Spanish striker Gonzalo Garcia on for Oscar Bobb. In the City ranks, Josko Gvardiol comes on for Nico O’Reilly.
 Share 29m ago 09.05 EST 74 min: Fulham win another corner as Khusanov swings a high boot to prevent Sessegnon from getting to a cross from the right to the far post. Shea Charles picks out Rodrigo Muniz with his inswinger but the Fulham striker is unable to steer the ball on target. Donnarumma gets booked for dissent after complaining to the referee about being blocked as he attempted to get to the ball.
 Share 33m ago 09.01 EST 72 min: Kenny Tete does superbly to stick out a leg for a well-timed tackle to prevent Jeremy Doku getting a shot on the turn away from near the penalty spot in the Fulham penalty area.
 Share 34m ago 08.59 EST 70 min: Fulham double-substitution: Hugo Larsson and Antonee Robinson come on for Josh King and Alex Iwobi. Manchester City substitution: Rayan Cherki replaces Phil Foden.
 Share 36m ago 08.57 EST 68 min: Donnarumma is forced into action again, saving a low Calvin Bassey shot from a tight angle with his legs. It’s a corner for Fulham , which Ruben Dias heads clear from Iwobi.
 Share 37m ago 08.56 EST 67 min: Oooof! Sander Berge plays Rodrigo Muniz in behind the City defence and the Fulham striker’s shot is saved by a big outstretched Donnarumma left hand.
 Share Updated at  08.58 EST 39m ago 08.54 EST 65 min: Haaland wins the race to a weighted through ball from Bouaddi and pulls the ball inside to Anderson. Hes first touch is sublime and tees up a low shot towards the far corner. The ball trundles inches wide of the upright.
 Share 41m ago 08.52 EST 63 min: I feel I might have been a little harsh in suggesting Bernd Leno should have done better for that Anderson goal. It was right in the corner.
 Share 43m ago 08.51 EST 61 min: The mood at the Etihad is improved immeasurably and Ryan Sessegnon is lucky to avoid a booking for a hold on Ndiaye that prevented the City winger from running on to a Haaland pass.
 Share Updated at  08.52 EST 45m ago 08.48 EST 59 min: That was an outstanding volley from Anderson, who watched the ball closely as it dropped his way from a headed clearnace. The contact couldn’t have been sweeter.
 Share Updated at  08.48 EST 47m ago 08.46 EST GOAL! Manchester City 1-1 Fulham (Anderson 58)
 Manchester City equalise! It’s a splendid finish from Elliot Anderson, who sends a low volley through a thicket of legs and under the dive of Leno from the edge of the penalty area, when the ball was cleared his way from a corner.
 View image in fullscreen Elliot Anderson blasts in the equaliser for City! Photograph: Molly Darlington/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Photograph: Molly Darlington/Getty Images Share Updated at  08.50 EST 48m ago 08.45 EST 56 min: Doku slips the ball to Bouaddi on the edge of the area but his shot is blocked by Affengruber, who is doing the defending of several men.
 Share 50m ago 08.44 EST 55 min: Ten minutes into the second half and City are showing no discernible signs of improvement following their abject first-half showing. It’s all far too easy for Fulham , who have not beaten City since 2009 and are trying to avoid their 21st consecutive defeat in all competitions at the hands of their hosts.
 Share 52m ago 08.42 EST 53 min: Fulham win a throw-in deep in City territory. They play it short and work the ball back to Calvin Bassey near the halfway line.
 Share 53m ago 08.41 EST 51 min: The ball breaks to Phil Foden in the Fulham penalty area but his shot is blocked out for a corner by David Affengruber, who appears to be having the game of his life. Nothing comes of the set-piece.
 Share 54m ago 08.39 EST 49 min: Fulham win a free-kick wide on the left and proceed to pen City deep inside their own half after the ball is swung into the penalty areas. City finally play the ball out despite assorted Fulham players snapping menacingly at their heels.
 Share 1h ago 08.37 EST 48 min: Give the people what they want – there’s a huge roar of approval from the stands as Haaland breaks into a sprint to press Leno as he deals with a backpass.
 Share 1h ago 08.35 EST Second half: Manchester City 0-1 Fulham
 46 min: Phil Foden gets the ball rolling for a City side that have, somewhat surprisingly, not made any changes during the break. Almost immediately they lose the ball to Oscar Bobb, whose delivery towards the City penalty area is headed away by Nico O’Reilly.
 Share 1h ago 08.29 EST That disallowed Haaland goal: According to Ifab Law 12 “A goalkeeper is considered to be in control of the ball with their hand(s)/arm(s) when: the ball is between their hands/arms or between their hand(s)/arm(s) and any surface (eg ground, own body.”
 Going by that and having seen several more replays, it’s this humble minute-by-minute reporter’s view that the decision to disallow Haaland’s effort was the correct one.
 Share Updated at  08.30 EST 1h ago 08.24 EST Some correspondence: “What a strange, but entertaining half,” writes Justin Kavanagh. “Haaland looks like he couldn’t buy a goal, while David Affengruber seems to be channeling his inner Bobby Moore in a Fulham shirt.”
 “Ref here,” writes Paul Pooley. “Two hands is not the standard. Control can be as little as one finger on the ball against the turf. The question is did Haaland play the ball when Leno had a hand on the ball against the ground.”
 “No doubt there’ll be focus on the disallowed goal (can see why not given, even if soft),” writes Shaun T. “But I also think it should be highlighted what an awful miss/bad connection from Haaland that was too. He had time to watch that Ndiaye cross right onto his foot and should really be burying that.”
 Share 1h ago 08.21 EST Manchester City 0-1 Fulham
 Half-time: Fulham lead courtesy of an excellent striked from Rodrigo Muniz, while City will feel they were unfairly denied an equaliser when Erling Haaland was penalised for bundling the ball over the line when Bernd Leno was in full control of it. It looked a harsh decision but the real story of this first half has revolved around how sluggish and off the pace City’s players have looked. Enzo Maresca has a big job on his hands if his side are to avoid their fourth consecutive top flight defeat.
 Share 1h ago 08.18 EST 45+2 min: The half ends with Bernd Leno saving easily from a half-hearted Jeremy Doku shot.
 Share 1h ago 08.17 EST 45+1 min: David Affengruber has been outstanding at the back for Fulham today and excels again here. He stands his ground to take the ball off Iliman Ndiaye’s toe after the City winger had jinked his way into the Fulham box and was about to unleash a shot.
 Share 1h ago 08.16 EST 44 min: With his arm in the air appealing for a free-kick that isn’t awarded, Nico O’Reilly completely switches off and allows Oscar Bobb to nip in behind him and shoot on goal from about eight yards out. Donnarumma denies the Fulham winger with an excellent save. That’s shocking – City are a mess!
 Share 1h ago 08.13 EST 41 min: Elliot Anderson advances towards the Fulham penalty area after winning the ball and plays a weighted pass to Nico O’Reilly. He eschews a shooting opportunity in favour of teeing up Haaland with a sideways pass but the Norwegian’s poor effort is way off-target. It takes a deflection to go out for a corner, from which nothing comes.
 Share 1h ago 08.11 EST 40 min: The City fans aren’t happy with their team’s extremely lacklustre performance and are jerring and whistling their players for not pressing Bernd Leno and assorted Fulham defenders as they pass the ball around the back.
 Share 1h ago 08.10 EST 37 min: City win a corner after good work from Jeremy Doku, who appeared to be fouled on the edge of the City area by Kenny Tete. From that set-piece, City win another. Phil Foden plays it short to Anderson near the edge of the penalty area but Fulham force their hosts backwards.
 Share 1h ago 08.07 EST 35 min: Erling Haaland sends a wild shot high and wide after running on to a beautifully weighted pass through the Fulham penalty area from Phil Foden.
 Share 1h ago 08.05 EST 33 min: Bernd Leno stands over the stationary ball after receiving a backpass and makes no effort to do anything with it, letting the clock tick down. Various City fans impatiently roar at Erling Haaland to press the German goalkeeper and force him into some sort of action.
 Share Updated at  08.06 EST 2h ago 08.03 EST 32 min: A Shea Charles cross from the right aimed towards Rodrigo Muniz is headed clear. Manchester City are looking very flat and vulnerable this afternoon.
 View image in fullscreen Sit down you’re rocking the boat… Photograph: MCFC/Getty Images Share Updated at  08.10 EST 2h ago 08.01 EST 30 min: A stray pass from Affengruber to Bassey is pounced on by Iliman Ndiaye near the halway line but a promising attack breaks down when Kenny Tete wins it back in the Fulham right-back area.
 Share 2h ago 07.59 EST 28 min: I think Fulham might have got away with one there, because Leno did have two hands on the ball at one point, he didn’t appear to have it under anything resembling control as Haaland bore down on him to force it over the line with his second attempt.
 Share 2h ago 07.58 EST 24 min: Iliman Ndiaye floats a superb cross into the Fulham penalty area from the right. Haaland connects with a thigh from about three yards out. Bernd Leno stops the ball only for the City striker to force the ball over the line with his follow-up. Haaland thinks he’s scored but his “goal” is disallowed because Leno is adjudged to have had two hands on the ball. Did he? I’m not so sure.
